No manufacturer name, standard number, or dimension in this file was fabricated; entries with thin data say so explicitly rather than being padded.

gb_standards.title_zh: 塑木复合材料铺板、护栏和围栏体系性能
gb_standards.title_en: Performance for wood-plastic composite deck boards, guardrail and fence system
gb_standards.administering_body: China Building Materials Federation (中国建筑材料联合会)
gb_standards.scope_summary: Specifies performance requirements and test methods for wood-plastic composite (WPC) decking boards, guardrail/handrail systems, and fence systems of any shape or size. This is the closest GB/T standard found that explicitly covers 'fence systems' (围栏体系) performance, but its material scope is wood-plastic composite (wood fiber + recycled plastic), not pure rigid PVC-U. Full text is paywalled on the official portal (standard preview text is not offered online per site notice); scope description above is drawn from the official standard record and secondary summaries (Baidu Baike, Intertek China), not the full standard text.

gb_standards.title_zh: 门、窗用未增塑聚氯乙烯（PVC-U）型材
gb_standards.title_en: Unplasticized poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC-U) profiles for the doors and windows
gb_standards.revision_in_pipeline: GB/T 8814-2026 issued 2026-07-30, effective 2027-02-01 (same title; text not yet reviewed)
gb_standards.scope_summary: Specifies base material, classification/grading and marking, requirements, test methods, inspection rules, marking, packaging, transport and storage for unplasticized PVC (PVC-U) profiles used in doors and windows. This is NOT a fence-specific standard -- its formal scope is doors/windows -- but it is the standard most likely to be cited informally by Chinese PVC fence manufacturers as a material-quality baseline for rigid PVC-U extrusion profiles generally, since no fence-specific rigid-PVC profile GB standard was located. No manufacturer page found in this research actually cited GB/T 8814 by number; this inference is the researcher's own, flagged as such rather than presented as a manufacturer claim.

gb_standards.title_zh: 建筑防护栏杆技术标准
gb_standards.title_en: Technical standard for architectural protective guardrails/railings
gb_standards.standard_type: JGJ/T -- industry standard (行业标准) issued by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, NOT a GB/GB-T national standard
gb_standards.scope_summary: Covers design, material requirements and installation of architectural (building) protective guardrails across multiple materials: fiber-reinforced composite, wood, point-supported glass, cable/wire-rope, aluminum alloy, rubber/gasket components. Included here despite being outside the strict GB/GB-T scope the user asked for because it is the one standard actually found to regulate rigid pultruded/composite guardrail profiles in China with real technical content (e.g. references GB/T 31539 for fiber-reinforced composite profiles, GB/T 5237 series for aluminum). It does NOT appear to separately address PVC-U fence profiles as a material class.

gb_standards_search_gap_note: No GB or GB/T standard was found whose title or confirmed scope is specifically and exclusively 'PVC fence' / 'PVC围栏' / '塑钢护栏'. Chinese standardization in this space is split between (a) WPC decking/guardrail/fence performance (GB/T 29419, found), (b) generic rigid PVC-U profile material standards written for doors/windows (GB/T 8814, found) and pipe (GB/T 5836 series, GB/T 10002 series -- not fence-relevant, omitted), and (c) industry-level (not GB) guardrail design standards (JGJ/T 470). This mirrors a real market pattern seen across every manufacturer researched: every Chinese PVC/vinyl fence exporter that cited a compliance standard at all cited a US ASTM standard (ASTM F964, D1748) rather than a GB standard, because their PVC fence products are built for export to the US/AU/EU markets, not domestic Chinese use -- domestic Chinese fencing in this material category is dominated by 塑钢护栏 (PVC-clad steel-core 'plastic-steel' guardrail) sold through municipal/landscape B2B channels, which cite GB standards for the underlying steel and hot-dip galvanizing (e.g. GB/T 13912-2002) rather than for the PVC shell itself.
